items_missed: 1_set_agenda: No 'How are you today?', no explicit agenda statement (what we'll cover + rough time), no 'sound good?' confirmation.

2_probe: No zip codes captured for either address, no stairs/floors question, no special considerations (narrow hallways/tight turns), no storage-stop question, no additional-stops question, no access/parking/HOA question, no moving-stressors question ('anything you're worried about?').

3_pricing: No itemized 'what's included' list (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap pads, bands, tools) beyond a vague 'everything is included,' no disassembly/reassembly mention (relevant since customer had bunk beds to disassemble), no No Worries Damage Coverage, no Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee, no full itemized no-hidden-fees pitch (no credit card fee/transportation fee/fuel surcharge/assembly fee callouts).
4_clock: Never explained clock mechanics at all — no on-site start point, no 2.5-hour minimum, no 15-minute prorated increments, no sense-check ('does that make sense?').

5_estimate: No stairs/elevator variable mentioned, no walk-distance variable, no equivalents used (school bus reference etc.), no assembly/disassembly named as a time variable despite bunk beds needing disassembly.

6_save_your_ass: No structured prep speech — no consolidation examples (kids' toys, garden tools, loose drawer items, wall photos), no 'take a carload' tip, no sense-check close. The only prep-adjacent moment was reactive: the customer proposed moving boxes himself and Jules simply agreed it would help, rather than proactively pitching prep as a cost-saver.

7_quote_booking: No 'reply with any corrections' ask to verify info, never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?' (customer had to prompt this himself), never gave branch hours or how to reach the office.
8_politeness: Never used the customer's name ('Jeff') a single time after he gave it, despite a 19.8-minute call.

9_bonus: No insurance explanation at all (No Worries + 60 cents/lb baseline) despite a gun safe and other big-ticket items being discussed; no rapport-building humor; some meandering cost time/organization (e.g., re-asked about washer/dryer after customer had already covered it).
top_strength: Jules adapted the plan live and collaboratively when the customer proposed self-moving some boxes to cut cost — recalculating cleanly from 6 guys/3 trucks down to 4 guys/2 trucks with an updated price range ($2,448–$3,264), and he pulled up the customer's real estate listing on his own to reference 'the gray sectional,' a genuine, unscripted rapport touch. He also extracted an extremely detailed room-by-room inventory over the phone despite starting down the virtual-walkthrough path.
coaching_note: You quoted and booked this one well on the fly, but you're leaving differentiators on the table — no Save Your Ass prep speech, no mention of No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, or the On-Time Guarantee, and you never explained the clock (2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments). Those are easy points and they build trust before the customer sees a bill. Also use the customer's name — Jeff gave it in the first 20 seconds and you never said it back to him once.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and transactional throughout with one standout rapport moment (noticing the listing photos), but otherwise scripted word choice ('Okay,' 'Got it,' 'No problem'), no empathy statements, and never used the customer's name.
